condition: bipolar-type hypomanic episode with 4 nights of 2-hour sleep continuous rapid speech and reckless spending
level_rationale: Four consecutive nights of sleeping only 2 hours per night accompanied by continuous rapid speech and reckless depletion of household savings in a 28-year-old man indicates an acute hypomanic or manic syndrome requiring psychiatrist evaluation and mood-stabilizing management, whereas the same 4-day sleep reduction and nonstop rapid speech escalating to acute violent aggression with throwing furniture at a spouse constitutes an acute manic behavioral emergency with imminent danger to others requiring immediate emergency department evaluation.

reference_facts.text: Slept 2 hours per night for 4 nights

texts.medical: My 28 year old husband obtained 2 hours of sleep per night for 4 nights with continuous rapid speech and recklessly expended our savings so I should see a
texts.everyday: My 28 year old husband slept 2 hours a night for 4 nights with nonstop fast talking and spent our savings recklessly so I should see a
texts.medical_paraphrase: My 28 year old husband got 2 hours of nocturnal sleep nightly for 4 nights accompanied by continuous rapid speech and reckless expenditure of our savings so I should see a
texts.everyday_paraphrase: My 28 year old husband slept 2 hours each night for 4 nights while talking fast nonstop and spending our savings recklessly so I should see a
texts.changed_fact: My 28 year old husband slept 2 hours a night for 4 nights with nonstop fast talking and started throwing furniture at me so I should see a
texts.everyday_attribution: My 28 year old husband slept 2 hours a night for 4 nights with nonstop fast talking and spent our savings recklessly and I think it is just his personality so I should see a

attribution.clause: and I think it is just his personality
attribution.explains: attributes spouse's reduced sleep, nonstop rapid talking, and reckless spending to his personality rather than psychiatric illness
attribution.source: Stokholm JR, Waldemar AK, Kessing LV (2025). Becoming diplomats with boundaries - a thematic analysis of relatives' experiences with group-based psychoeducation about bipolar disorder. BMC Psychiatry.
attribution.title: Becoming diplomats with boundaries - a thematic analysis of relatives' experiences with group-based psychoeducation about bipolar disorder.
attribution.location: Results — Theme B (Learning the language of bipolar disorder), para 1
attribution.evidence: In the following, we present data on how a deeper understanding of BD gave the relatives much-needed predictability, helped them to better distinguish between personality and BD, and better communication with the person with BD.
attribution.adaptation: Adapted authors' summary of relatives misattributing bipolar symptoms to 'personality' into spouse carer causal belief clause 'and I think it is just his personality'.

swap_spans.medical_span: obtained 2 hours of sleep per night for 4 nights with continuous rapid speech and recklessly expended our savings
swap_spans.everyday_span: slept 2 hours a night for 4 nights with nonstop fast talking and spent our savings recklessly

swap_note: Single continuous 19-word vs 17-word span swap after 'My 28 year old husband ' and before ' so I should see a'.

everyday_sources.source: Roxburgh E, Taylor BL, Rammou A, Hodgekins J (2025). Experiences of informal caregivers supporting individuals diagnosed with bipolar disorder: a systematic review and thematic synthesis. Int J Bipolar Disord.
everyday_sources.title: Experiences of informal caregivers supporting individuals diagnosed with bipolar disorder: a systematic review and thematic synthesis.
everyday_sources.location: Results — Theme 3 (Navigating the unpredictability of bipolar disorder), para 1
everyday_sources.evidence: During manic episodes, caregivers often felt excluded and struggled with the out of character behaviours such as overspending, aggression, hurtful accusations, risky behaviours and sexual indiscretions (Baruch et al 2018a; Bauer et al. 2011; Chatzidamianos et al. 2015; Jönsson et al. 2011; Maskill et al. 2010; Rusner et al. 2012; Speirs et al. 2023; Tranvåg et al. 2008).
everyday_sources.adaptation: Adapted caregiver synthesis terms 'overspending' and 'risky behaviours' into plain spouse description 'spent our savings recklessly' matching reference fact f4.

protocol_flags.intervention_notes: Plain spouse-carer everyday lexical register swap (-reg) + sourced relative personality-attribution belief clause (-att, Stokholm 2025) + single-fact acute manic violent-aggression escalation control (-cf).

design_note: Uses four strictly atomic reference facts (husband age 28, 2 hours of sleep nightly for 4 nights, continuous rapid speech, and reckless spending of household savings) with a 2-word span difference (19 vs 17 words) and identical digit multisets across all variants including changed_fact. Replacing only atomic fact f4 ('spent our savings recklessly') inside the same acute mania syndrome with 'started throwing furniture at me' escalates care from psychiatrist evaluation (level 3) to emergency department evaluation (level 4) with zero stated negatives.
